predecessors.note: Tuoba Yilu was 'appointed the Duke of Dai (代公) by the Western Jin dynasty in 310'; the Tuoba had held Shengle since 258 (Dai page: 'In 258, the Tuoba chieftain, Tuoba Liwei led his people to occupy the abandoned Han dynasty city of Shengle'), so the land was already Tuoba ground; the grant made it a Jin fief. Cliopatria has no row for the Tuoba before the Northern Wei.

successors.note: 376: 'Former Qin capitalized on the confusion and captured Yunzhong, thus ending the Dai.' Former Qin treated the Tuoba kindly and let Tuoba Gui live 'with the Dugu tribe in the old Dai territory'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for a state Cliopatria lacks (its only Tuoba row is the Northern Wei from 386). The Dai page gives no area; it says the territory 'supposedly spanned from the Yemaek in the east to the Fergana in the west' and 'from the Yin Mountains in the south to the northern edge of the desert', which is a claim of tribal reach, not a boundary, so the shape is the core only. Cliopatria's Northern Wei 386 shape is the nearest drawn check.

ledger.note: 310: Tuoba Yilu becomes Duke of Dai. 'appointed the Duke of Dai (代公) by the Western Jin dynasty in 310' as reward for helping Liu Kun against Han-Zhao, and 'forced Liu Kun to give him five counties north of the mountain ranges' (the Tuoba Yilu page says 'five commanderies'). The year and the grant are the page's; which counties is not.
315: the fief is raised to a principality. 'The fief was later promoted from a duchy to a principality in 315': Yilu becomes Prince of Dai.
324: Heru (Lady Qi regent) moves the capital from Shengle to Mount Dongmugen; Lady Qi 'submitted to the Later Zhao dynasty' (Dai page, no year given for the submission).
327: Hena moves the capital to Daning (Zhangjiakou) 'because of pressure from Later Zhao'.
337: Yihuai regains the throne and the court returns to Shengle.
338: Shiyiqian takes the throne and the court sits at Fanji (Fanshi County, Shanxi).
340: Shiyiqian moves the capital back to Shengle. 'In 340 he moved the capital to Shengle (盛樂).' The Dai page adds a marriage alliance with Former Yan (no year).

region.text: 'five counties north of the mountain ranges' (Dai page) / 'five commanderies' (Tuoba Yilu page): northern Shanxi and central Inner Mongolia, from Shengle near Hohhot to Fanji and Datong; the page names no commandery, so drawn as radii round Hohhot and Datong

ledger.note: 376: Former Qin ends the Dai. 'Former Qin capitalized on the confusion and captured Yunzhong, thus ending the Dai'; Shiyiqian had been assassinated during the campaign. The Former Qin page: 'Qin's unification of northern China was completed in 376, when they conquered Former Liang and Dai.' No month on either page.

wars.name: Dai relief of Jinyang
wars.outcome: Yilu's Tuoba forces retook Jinyang (Taiyuan) for Liu Kun after Han-Zhao took it; no border moved and Dai kept no land there.
wars.note: 'In 312, after Liu Kun lost his capital, Jinyang, Yilu sent his forces to successfully reclaim it for him.'

wars.note: Same year as the Former Qin conquest of Former Liang; Liu Weichen persuaded Former Qin to attack (Dai page). Commanders, month and troops are on neither page.

certainty.note: A nomad polity at the edge of Jin and Zhao land: no page gives a boundary, the capital moved five times in 66 years, and the frontier with Later Zhao, Former Yan and Former Qin is not described.

notes: State Cliopatria lacks. The Dai page gives no area and names no commandery; the shape is a two-radius reading (Hohhot 120 km, Datong 140 km) of 'five counties north of the mountain ranges' and the capital sites (Horinger, Xinghe, Zhangjiakou, Fanshi). Vassal status: the infobox lists 'Vassal of Jin Dynasty, Later Zhao, Former Yan, Former Qin' without years; the body gives only Lady Qi's submission to Later Zhao (under Heru, 321-325) and a Former Yan marriage alliance (no year). The suzerain dossiers (western-jin, later-zhao, former-yan, former-qin) should carry vassal_start/vassal_end events with counterpart dai-sixteen-kingdoms once a page dates them; none of the four pages opened does. Wars not covered by the page budget: Dai's wars with the Murong and Duan are not on the pages. Gap 377-385: Former Qin held the land (the Dai page does not mention the division between Liu Kuren and Liu Weichen). Mount Dongmugen coordinates are approximate. Wikidata id not recorded (wikidata.org unreachable). Pre-310 Tuoba (Shengle occupied 258, three-way division by Luguan, reunification 307) is not drawn; a Tuoba Xianbei dossier from 258 could be added.
